A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SPATIA and MIST, retaining identifiable architecture, datasets, and experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original annotation, clustering, biomarker prediction, gene prediction, image generation, component-ablation, and token-merging results.

after.justification: v2 retains original predictive results and reports additional conditional-generation comparisons, cross-platform clustering, robustness experiments, and computational profiling.

M1.justification: v1's conditional diffusion generator and inference-time token merging are replaced by control-to-target flow matching using weak optimal-transport pairs, confidence weighting, transition signatures, condition-contrastive regularization, and morphology-profile alignment. v2 also introduces platform-specific tokens and additional representation-training objectives. The hierarchical multimodal backbone remains recognizable.

E1.justification: MIST expands from 49 Xenium sources to 74 sources covering Xenium, CosMx, Stereo-seq, and Visium HD, including SEA-AD and SPATCH additions. v2 adds cross-platform clustering and explicit breast-cancer progression and immune-remodeling generation scenarios. The MS, aortic single-cell, BCNB, and five HEST cancer-cohort evaluations remain.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 introduces evaluated generation comparisons with CellFlux, MorphDiff, and GeneFlow, whereas v1's generation table contains only SPATIA. New platform-clustering comparisons include scFoundation, Nicheformer, and UCE. Existing predictive comparator sets are retained, including UNIv1.5 in the HEST figure despite its omission from v2's baseline prose.

E3.justification: v1 evaluates image reconstruction using PSNR and SSIM; v2 evaluates weakly paired control-to-target distributions using FID, KID, and CellProfiler-derived Wasserstein/KS measures. Appendix C specifies a new pairing protocol, including a 50-cell minimum per state and 1,584 constructed pairs. New platform experiments evaluate frozen embeddings separately on Xenium and CosMx.

E4.justification: v2 adds confidence-reweighting and morphology-loss ablations, niche-context and cell-only generation controls, retraining with 10% and 20% corrupted OT pairs, and batch-mixing visualizations against PCA. The cumulative classification ablation is retained as Table 5. v1's token-merging efficiency comparison is removed.

E5.justification: v1 already shows HEST error bars but does not specify run counts. v2 reports three runs, biomarker standard deviations below 0.01 for AUC and 0.012 for balanced accuracy, and separately states 3–4 seeds with standard deviation ±0.05 in Appendix A. These are additional reporting disclosures; an increase in runs is not established.

E6.justification: v2 adds generation, platform-clustering, and robustness results, including full-generator FID 58.5 and KID 2.01. v1's cross-modal Table 3 results and 37% generation-speedup finding disappear. Matched HEST plot values change, including IDC 59.93 to 60.08 and LUAD 57.54 to 57.82 on the plotted scale. Original cell-benchmark and classification-ablation values remain unchanged. The new generation scores use different conditions and metrics.

T1.justification: v2 introduces formal OT couplings, normalized confidence weights, transition signatures, latent interpolation bridges, and weighted/contrastive flow objectives, replacing v1's CFG and token-merging formalism. This is substantial new mathematical content without new theorems. Appendix C.2 also introduces an entropy-sign inconsistency between its OT objective and stated Sinkhorn solution.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes efficient token-merged diffusion and bidirectional inference. v2 makes platform invariance and weakly supervised, spatially conditioned phenotype transitions central contributions. Its abstract, introduction, and conclusion introduce quantified claims of 8% generative-fidelity improvement and predictive gains up to 3%, alongside the expanded multiplatform MIST contribution.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly interprets weak pairs as population-level transitions rather than observations of the same cell before and after perturbation. It adds explanations of pairing-noise robustness, spatial conditioning, batch invariance, and leakage prevention. The new Impact Statement limits outputs to predictive simulations without experimental validation and excludes direct clinical decision-making.

D1.justification: v2 adds localized-batching descriptions, downstream learning rates and layer-selection details, donor-disjoint split disclosure, staining and resizing/padding instructions, pairing/QC documentation, and a four-H100 training profile of approximately 30 hours. These disclosures do not establish changes to previously unspecified settings. The backbone hyperparameter table is retained; diffusion-specific implementation documentation is replaced by OT/pairing material.

R1.justification: v2 substantially redirects positioning toward flow matching, optimal transport, and biological perturbation modeling, adding foundational and application references including CellFlux, GeneFlow, CellFlow, and NicheFlow. It also adds spatial-integration comparisons such as SpaGCN and STAligner while removing much diffusion-acceleration literature. The existing single-cell review moves to Appendix D rather than disappearing.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and method narrative are extensively rewritten. Problem formulation is integrated into the model section, self-supervised objectives and single-cell related work move to appendices, and experiments are reordered around generation and platform evaluation. The title and appendix organization also change.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one to two columns, with redesigned overview diagrams and new generation, platform, robustness, and computational displays. v1 Figure 3 is retained as v2 Figure 2. The HEST chart is redrawn as Figure 6 with its vertical axis starting at zero instead of 20, while retained tables are relocated and reformatted.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's largely uncomparative generation evidence, v2 adds competing generators, component controls, and pairing-noise tests, making its generative contribution easier to assess. Run disclosures and explicit simulation limitations also help. These benefits are tempered by problems in the new central material: the OT entropy-sign inconsistency, unclear higher-is-better KS interpretation, and overly broad platform-superiority language despite CosMx NMI of 0.497 versus scFoundation's 0.548. The evidence supports a limited net quality improvement.
